text: When Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, heard that Abner had died at Hebron, his hands went limp, and all Israel was shaken.

versions.text: When Saul's son heard that Abner had died at Hebron, his hands went limp, and all Israel was shaken.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads only "Saul's son," which leaves the oral hearer without a referent at the opening of the chapter; naming Ish-bosheth (as the following verses do) aids clarity for reading aloud. A footnote could note that the Hebrew has simply "Saul's son."

text: Saul's son had two men who were commanders of raiding bands. One was named Baanah and the other Rechab; they were sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, of the tribe of Benjamin—for Beeroth too was reckoned as belonging to Benjamin.
The people of Beeroth had fled to Gittaim, and they have lived there as foreigners to this day.

Now Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son who was crippled in both feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she hurried away, he fell and was left lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, set out and came to the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while he was taking his midday rest.
They came right inside the house while the wheat was being taken in, and they struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah slipped away.

versions.text: They came inside the house as though to fetch wheat, and they struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah slipped away.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew does not contain a word of pretense ("as though"); לֹקְחֵי חִטִּים is a difficult phrase best rendered without importing a motive. A footnote noting the difficulty of the Hebrew here would also help the reader.

text: They had entered the house while he lay on his bed in his bedroom, and they struck him down and killed him. They cut off his head, took it with them, and traveled all night by way of the Arabah.

They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life. Today the LORD has avenged my lord the king on Saul and his offspring."
But David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from every distress—
when a man told me, 'Saul is dead,' thinking he was bringing good news, I seized him and killed him at Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news!
How much more, when wicked men have murdered an innocent man in his own house, on his own bed—shall I not now require his blood from your hands and rid the land of you?"

versions.text: How much more, when wicked men have murdered an innocent man in his own house, on his own bed—shall I not now require his blood from your hands and rid the earth of you?"
versions.explanation: הָאָרֶץ here refers to the land (of Israel), not the whole earth; David is speaking of purging these men from his kingdom. "Land" is both more accurate and reads naturally aloud.

text: So David gave the order to his men, and they killed them. They cut off their hands and feet and hung the bodies beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in Abner's tomb at Hebron.
